title: Reflexivity and intersection of height-one localizations over a normal domain
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] with fraction field $K$, and let $M$ be a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Write $M_K=K\otimes_A M$. A module is torsion free if $am=0$ with $0\ne a\in A$ implies $m=0$. It is reflexive if the evaluation map $M\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,A),A)$, sending $m$ to $(\varphi\mapsto\varphi(m))$, is an isomorphism. Let $H(A)$ be the set of nonzero prime ideals $\mathfrak p$ having no prime strictly between $(0)$ and $\mathfrak p$. For $\mathfrak p\in H(A)$, write $M_{\mathfrak p}=(A\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}M$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Then $M$ is reflexive if and only if it is torsion free and, identifying $M$ and every $M_{\mathfrak p}$ with their images in $M_K$, one has $M=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\in H(A)}M_{\mathfrak p}$. An intersection over an empty set means all of $M_K$.

source.place: Tag 0AVB, more-algebra-lemma-reflexive-over-normal, equivalence of conditions (1) and (3), statement and proof at lines 5578-5630.

proof.text: First establish the scalar test needed below. If $x=a/b\in K$, $b\ne0$, lies in every $A_{\mathfrak p}$ with $\mathfrak p\in H(A)$, every associated prime of $A/bA$ has height one by [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-principal-quotient-associated-height]. At each such prime write $x=c/s$ with $s\notin\mathfrak p$. The equality $sa=bc$ in the domain gives $s\bar a=0$ in $A/bA$. The equivalent annihilator formulation of [lem-weil-pbc-module-injects-localizations-associated-primes] gives $\bar a=0$. Thus $a\in bA$ and $x\in A$; the reverse inclusion is immediate. This proves $A=\bigcap_{H(A)}A_{\mathfrak p}$, also when there are no height-one primes, since the associated-prime test permits an empty set.

source.place: Tag 031T, lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1, proof of (2), using Tag 0311, lemma-zero-at-ass-zero.

proof.text: Put $M^*=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,A)$ and $\eta_M(m)(\varphi)=\varphi(m)$. For generators $m_1,\ldots,m_t$ of $M$, the map $M^*\to A^t$, $\varphi\mapsto(\varphi(m_i))_i$, is injective: its kernel consists of functionals vanishing on every generator. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] makes $M^*$ finite. The module $M^{**}$ is torsion free: $az=0$, $a\ne0$, implies $az(\varphi)=0$ in the domain $A$ for every $\varphi$, so $z=0$. By [lem-per-torsion-free-bidual-injective], $\eta_M$ is injective exactly when $M$ is torsion free. In particular reflexivity implies torsion freeness. By the zero criterion for fractions [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], a torsion-free module injects into its localization at $A\setminus\{0\}$; its prime localizations likewise embed there by $m/s\mapsto m/s$.

source.place: Tag 0AV0, lemma-reflexive-torsion-free, (1) and (3); finite dual by Algebra Tag 00IK, lemma-Noetherian-basic.

proof.text: For $B=K$ or $A_{\mathfrak p}$, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base], with both base rings equal to $A$ and its module $M$ there equal to $A$, identifies $B\otimes_A T$ with $S^{-1}T$ for any $A$-module $T$: $(a/s)\otimes t\mapsto at/s$, with inverse $t/s\mapsto(1/s)\otimes t$. Here $S=A\setminus\{0\}$ or $A\setminus\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], $A\to B$ is flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented] first to $(M,A)$, then to $(M^*,A)$; its Noetherian finite-module clause applies by Step 2. This gives $(M^*)_B\simeq(M_B)^*$ and $(M^{**})_B\simeq(M_B)^{**}$. Explicitly $\varphi/s$ acts on $m/t$ by $\varphi(m)/(st)$, and $z/s$ acts on $\varphi/t$ by $z(\varphi)/(st)$. Thus these identifications send $\eta_M(m)/s$ to $\eta_{M_B}(m/s)$, and further passage from $A_{\mathfrak p}$ to $K$ has the same formulas.

source.place: Tag 087R, lemma-pseudo-coherence-and-base-change-ext, (1) and final sentence; Algebra Tags 00HT and 00DL for flat localization and tensor localization.

proof.text: For later use, evaluation is an isomorphism on every finite free module $F$ over a commutative ring $B$. If $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ is a basis with coordinate functionals $\epsilon_i$, its inverse sends $z\in F^{**}$ to $\sum_i z(\epsilon_i)e_i$: for $\lambda\in F^*$ the identity $\lambda=\sum_i\lambda(e_i)\epsilon_i$ gives both inverse identities. This includes $r=0$. The images of the finite generators of $M$ generate $V=M_K$ over $K$, so [lem-per-division-ring-finite-basis], applied to the field $K$, gives a finite basis of $V$. Consequently $\eta_V$ is an isomorphism by the displayed formula. Since $M^{**}$ is torsion free, it injects into $(M^{**})_K$ by Step 2. Combining Step 3 with $\eta_V^{-1}$ therefore embeds $M^{**}$ into $V$, and sends $\eta_M(m)$ to $m/1$. If $M$ is torsion free this identifies $M\subseteq M^{**}\subseteq V$.

source.place: Tag 0AV0, lemma-reflexive-torsion-free, proof: generic finite-dimensional evaluation; the finite-free evaluation formula is written out here.

proof.text: Suppose $M$ is reflexive, hence torsion free by [lem-per-torsion-free-bidual-injective]. If $v\in V$ lies in every $M_{\mathfrak p}$, every $\varphi\in M^*$ satisfies $\varphi_K(v)\in A_{\mathfrak p}$ for every $\mathfrak p\in H(A)$, by the fractions formula in Step 3. Step 1 gives $\varphi_K(v)\in A$. Thus $z(\varphi)=\varphi_K(v)$ defines an $A$-linear element $z\in M^{**}$. Its image in $V$ under Step 4 is $v$: on a general rational functional $\varphi/s\in(M^*)_K=V^*$ both evaluate as $\varphi_K(v)/s$. Reflexivity supplies $m\in M$ with $\eta_M(m)=z$, whence $v=m/1$. The inclusion $M\subseteq M_{\mathfrak p}$ for every prime is given by $m\mapsto m/1$. This proves the required intersection equality.

source.place: Tag 0AVB, lemma-reflexive-over-normal, (1) implies (3); agent dual-evaluation expansion using Algebra Tag 031T(2) instead of the intermediate S2-module criterion.

proof.text:
Now assume $M$ is torsion free and has the asserted intersection equality. For $\mathfrak p\in H(A)$ put $B=A_{\mathfrak p}$. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], a normal domain with fraction field $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], and local by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Its Krull dimension is one by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime]: a prime $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ satisfies $(0)\subseteq\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak p$, hence $\mathfrak q=(0)$ by the definition of $H(A)$, so the longest chain ending inside $\mathfrak p$ is $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$. Hence [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] makes $B$ a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. The module $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is finite, generated by $m_i/1$. It is torsion free over $A_{\mathfrak p}$: if $(a/t)(m/s)=0$ and $a/t

source.place: Tag 0AVB, lemma-reflexive-over-normal, proof of (3) implies (1), using Tag 0AUW, lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat, (3), Algebra Tag 031T proof of (3) ($R_1$ for a Noetherian normal domain, Tag 031S lemma-criterion-normal) and Algebra Tag 00PD.

proof.text: For $z\in M^{**}$ let $v\in V$ be its image from Step 4. For every height-one prime the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-hom-finitely-presented] applied twice, as in Step 3, carries $z/1$ into $(M_{\mathfrak p})^{**}$. By Step 6 it equals $\eta_{M_{\mathfrak p}}(m_{\mathfrak p})$ for some $m_{\mathfrak p}\in M_{\mathfrak p}$. The explicit evaluation formulas of Step 3 show that its image in $V$ is the image of $m_{\mathfrak p}$, so $v\in M_{\mathfrak p}$ for every such prime. The assumed intersection equality gives $v=m/1$ for some $m\in M$. The embedding $M^{**}\hookrightarrow V$ then gives $z=\eta_M(m)$. Thus $\eta_M$ is surjective; it is injective by [lem-per-torsion-free-bidual-injective], hence is an isomorphism. If $H(A)$ is empty the same reasoning uses the assumed equality $M=V$ and has no local conditions to check.
